title: Microsoft 365 Copilot offer and name updates
summary: Starting October 16, 2026, Microsoft 365 Copilot subscriptions requiring a base Microsoft 365 subscription will include "(add-on)" in their names. From December 1, 2026, new subscriptions can be purchased without this requirement and won't have "(add-on)" in their names. Existing subscriptions remain unchanged except for the name update. No migration is needed.
body:
[What and Why:]

We're updating Microsoft 365 Copilot subscription names to make purchasing requirements clearer.

Beginning October 16, 2026, existing Microsoft 365 Copilot subscriptions that require a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription will include "(add-on)" in their names. Examples include Microsoft 365 Copilot (add-on) and Microsoft 365 Copilot Business (add-on).

The "(add-on)" designation reflects the qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription requirement for these existing subscriptions. Beginning December 1, 2026, new Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscriptions can be purchased without a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription. 

[Rollout Schedule:]

- October 16, 2026: Microsoft 365 Copilot subscriptions that require a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription will include "(add-on)" in their names.- December 1, 2026: New Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscriptions can be purchased without a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription and will not include "(add-on)" in their names.- December 1, 2026: Existing add-on subscriptions will reach end of sale for new purchases. This is not end of life: You can continue to renew your subscriptions and add or reduce seats as you do today.- Existing subscriptions will retain "(add-on)" in their names.[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

- Organizations with Microsoft 365 Copilot or Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscriptions that require a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription.Platforms/Services:

- Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscriptions.What will happen:

- Existing subscriptions that require a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription will be renamed: - Microsoft 365 Copilot (add-on)- Microsoft 365 Copilot Business (add-on)- Your subscription, service, pricing, licensing rights, and renewal eligibility remain unchanged.- No migration or license reassignment is required.- The name update does not change Copilot capabilities, which continue to depend on the apps and services you're licensed for.- Self-service purchase (SSP) and end-user trials within Microsoft 365 products will continue to be available with this update.- Beginning December 1, 2026, new subscriptions without the qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription requirement will be available without "(add-on)" in their names.[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required for most organizations.

- Do not migrate subscriptions or reassign licenses solely because of the name update.- If you use PowerShell scripts or license management processes that reference product names, update them to use product or SKU IDs before October 16, 2026.- Consider updating internal documentation that references the current subscription names.[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.
bodyHtml:
[What and Why:]

We're updating Microsoft 365 Copilot subscription names to make purchasing requirements clearer.

Beginning October 16, 2026, existing Microsoft 365 Copilot subscriptions that require a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription will include "(add-on)" in their names. Examples include Microsoft 365 Copilot (add-on) and Microsoft 365 Copilot Business (add-on).

The "(add-on)" designation reflects the qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription requirement for these existing subscriptions. Beginning December 1, 2026, new Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscriptions can be purchased without a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription. 

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • October 16, 2026:

    Microsoft 365 Copilot subscriptions that require a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription will include "(add-on)" in their names.

  • December 1, 2026:

    New Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscriptions can be purchased without a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription and will not include "(add-on)" in their names.

  • December 1, 2026:

    Existing add-on subscriptions will reach end of sale for new purchases. This is not end of life: You can continue to renew your subscriptions and add or reduce seats as you do today.

  • Existing subscriptions will retain "(add-on)" in their names.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Organizations with Microsoft 365 Copilot or Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscriptions that require a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscriptions.

What will happen:

  • Existing subscriptions that require a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription will be renamed: 

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot (add-on)

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot Business (add-on)

  • Your subscription, service, pricing, licensing rights, and renewal eligibility remain unchanged.

  • No migration or license reassignment is required.

  • The name update does not change Copilot capabilities, which continue to depend on the apps and services you're licensed for.

  • Self-service purchase (SSP) and end-user trials within Microsoft 365 products will continue to be available with this update.

  • Beginning December 1, 2026, new subscriptions without the qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription requirement will be available without "(add-on)" in their names.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required for most organizations.

  • Do not migrate subscriptions or reassign licenses solely because of the name update.

  • If you use PowerShell scripts or license management processes that reference product names, update them to use product or SKU IDs before

    October 16, 2026.

  • Consider updating internal documentation that references the current subscription names.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.
